required_source.actual_result_applied: fractional-potential interface and physical square peel

partner.actual_application: R0=2(x1*y1+x2*y2) gives density cap 2*sqrt(pi); adding curvature to both active banks crosses the partner theorem boundary and yields the exact divergent-density obstruction, while the new half-Riesz receiver remains finite.

new_results.statement: For R=F(X_I)+2 X_I^T M X_J+G(X_J)+c with disjoint original independent banks, arbitrary same-bank phases, and rank-two M with nonzero singular values sigma1,sigma2, H_{1/2}(R)<=8(sigma1 sigma2)^(-1/4).
new_results.mechanism: twisted product-projection L2 caps plus bilateral two-dimensional Plancherel, then half-Riesz weighted frequency integration

new_results.statement: For a nonzero original physical pivot a whose exact Schur residual has a rank-two physical cross block with singular values sigma1,sigma2, ||p_Q||inf<=8|a|^(-1/2)(sigma1 sigma2)^(-1/4).

For an exact rank-three original-coordinate cross block with singular values sigma1,sigma2,sigma3, arbitrary self-curvature on both banks is allowed and ||p_Q||inf<=6(sigma1 sigma2 sigma3)^(-1/3); the characteristic function is L1 and the density has a continuous representative.
For five disjoint normalized banks, Q_m=(A+C)^2-(B-D)^2+W^2 has spectrum {2,-2,1}, physical diagonals 1/m, pair determinants <=1/m^2, and ||p_Qm||inf<=8sqrt(2) for all cap-one product laws.

new_correction.summary: R=(x1+y1)^2-(x2-y2)^2 with iid Uniform[-1/2,1/2] has cross block I2 yet p_R(0)=infinity. This refutes direct bounded density from rank-two cross currency when both active banks keep arbitrary curvature; it is not a QFORM counterexample because only eigenvalues 2,-2 are large.
